newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa in critical condition -- doctors.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa in critical condition -- doctors.

text.p: Mother Teresa was in critical condition on Sunday and long-standing lung and renal diseases forced doctors to postpone treatment with drugs to correct an irregular heart rhythm, a medical bulletin said.
"Mother Teresa up to this moment remains in critical condition," the bulletin, issued at 12.45 p.m. (0715 GMT), said.

"Even though the ischaemia of the heart has been corrected, her heart rhythm is still irregular. Her long-standing lung and renal diseases continue to be a major concern, which could complicate heart condition and recovery," it added.
A.K. Chatterjee, administrator of the B.M. Birla Heart Research Centre in Calcutta, told reporters doctors had postponed treatment of her irregular heart rhythm with drugs.
A bulletin issued earlier on Sunday by the centre said her condition was stable and that she was "comfortable and cheerful".

Mother Teresa, the 86-year-old Roman Catholic missionary, known as the "Saint of the Gutters" for her work with the world's poor, underwent surgery on Friday to remove blockages in two coronary arteries.
